title: Deck – Phone Control Panel for Coding Agents
tools: Python (aiohttp) · tmux · Rust (iroh peer-to-peer tunnel) · Android (Capacitor) · Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi
blurb: A web app on each PC that lets a phone start, watch and message coding agents, which keep running in tmux when the phone sleeps.
long: Deck runs on each of my PCs (personal computers) and gives my phone a tab per agent session, with one-tap keys for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and others. Each agent runs in its own tmux session, so closing the phone or losing signal never stops it.

Agents show up as a chat rather than a raw terminal, with expandable tool calls and questions turned into buttons. All my PCs join one Deck with no main host; the phone app fails over after 4 s, and chats can move between hosts mid-conversation.
The server only listens on localhost and is reached over Tailscale or a built-in peer-to-peer tunnel. New devices pair with a one-time 5-minute code approved from a paired device.
highlights: Six agent types plus custom scripts, each in its own tmux session
